story_text.value:
Hi guys. I had an idea to wrote API and some nice WebUI for Fdroid private feed for Android APKs for quite some time. I have some internal applications that I want to share with my family (i.e. smart home management app). First I had just bunch of static files that were managed by my GitLab instance but at some point it broke.

Then with growing number of applications and packages and no possibility of managing them easily (I think Fdroid tools are unnecessarily complicated) it was too much to do by hand. With coding agents I decided to try it out and write an application entirely by agent (as kind of experiment) it was usable but quite buggy. And costly.

After that I fixed bugs with local model, cleaned up code, added tests, tested it for few weeks myself with Fdroid clients on multiple phones and other devices. It is working and I decided to share it with community.

It us an API wrapping Fdroid python packages for managing Fdroid feed, signing APKs and etc. It supports API keys that I am feeding to my CI to upload new APKs after the build. It allows to:

- add, update and remove applications

- manages their keys so you do not have to

- allows to add description and icons

- allows to add (with release changes) and remove releases of applications

- manages versions of next release

It is designed to be integrated with SSO of your choice, because having SSO for your self hosted applications seems much better idea than each of local applications to manage it itself.

Links:

https://github.com/npodbielski/FdroidManager

https://hub.docker.com/r/npodbielski/fdroidmgr/tags

I hope it can be of use for more people.

story_text.value:
I look up a lot at the sky at night and made this because I wanted to better understand what is up there.

Orbital shows all 32,000+ tracked objects at their current positions: about 17,000 working satellites, 2,800 dead ones, 2,200 spent rocket bodies and 10,700 pieces of debris.

Each is color coded, can be switched off, and can be "clicked" to follow. For the well-known ones it pulls up a real photo (where available), what it is for, and when it stopped working.

There is an animation that shows launch history from 1957 to today. When you first visit, click on the "Watch 1957 → today" button to see the animation.

You can also "fly out" to the solar system and see the planets, moons, comets and spacecraft further out there.

My orbit data comes from Space-Track. I also pull from CelesTrak to determine which satellites are currently active.

It is a static site on GitHub Pages (currently) with no backend, no accounts, and no ads. It also installs as an app and reopens offline.

I wrote it with Claude Code doing most of the implementation. I will provide the link to the source if you want it.

I would like to hear what you think about it. Specifically, what is confusing on a first visit, and what would make you come back to it. And anything else constructive you would like to share.

title.value: Show HN: Orbital – Everything (known) in Earth orbit, live in 3D, in the browser

story_text.value:
Hello! Looking to share forbear, a immediate mode GUI library that looks like the web, has a React-like DX and is as fast as possible.

I've already built a real program (https://github.com/gabrielmfern/calculator) to stress it, and the binary is only 3.6MB, the first frame shows up in ~300ms, it uses 10.5MB of working set memory, and it's all 1,155 lines of code.

It can be used with Jai (Jonathan Blow's private beta programming language), and also from C or any C-compatible language.

On Linux and macOS:

  curl -fsSL https://forbear.dev/quick-start.sh | sh
On Windows:

  irm https://www.forbear.dev/quick-start.ps1 | iex
It's missing basic features like accessibility, input method support, and built-in text input primitives.

It has a LICENSE that makes it source available. It's free for nonprofits, open source software or internal tools, but, it charges a capped 1% royalty for any company that exceeds a revenue threshold.

I would love to hear feedback, specially on the new C API as I am not very experienced with C.

Thanks!

title.value: Show HN: Forbear is a immediate mode GUI library that looks like the web

story_text.value:
We all use different agentic systems, bots, chats, and so on. One day I realized that I need to copy context between the apps. It is annoying.

So I created a trivial local MCP which sits on top of SQLite and exposes Cypher so LLM can query anything. Also LLM can define a schema if it understands it needs new nodes or edges.

How do I use it: 1. I've scanned all my documents and stored passports, driver licences and all kind of contracts for my apartment, insurance and so on. And not only mine - the entire family. 2. I've extracted all the key date and values. Also gemini extracted all the personal relations. Like "Alex is-a-child-of Bob". "Bob is-married-to Anna". So i can ask "give me a passport number of my son" and it gives it back instantly. It might not be a big deal, but it is very convenient. 3. It stores all the projects I'm working on, key steps and decisions. 4. And the most important thing - it works from anywhere. I can ask Hermes i telegram to remind me when my insurance ends or I can reference my project in ClaudeCode just by name and it will get the entire history from Antigravity.

I would be happy if you guys find it useful.

story_text.value:
This open-source TUI and CLI allows running the workflows that android devs run every day without leaving the terminal and each one in their own worktree.

You can see the agents working in a control pane with different status. The TUI will inform you when it needs your help.

You can: 1. Create a Pull Request from a ticket, the harness does a plan -> code -> review workflow. You can decide the model per state. 2. Auto fix the ticket comments, the harness fetches the PR comments and show it in the dashboard. You can previsualize and approve or request a new fix. 3. Review the diff, the TUI has a beauty diff viewer so you can review the code without leaving the terminal. 4. Open the worktree in Android Studio or claude code directly from the TUI. 5. Permission and budget management: you can auto approve comments or approve once. You can also set a spend limit per stage.

It is optimized for android: 1. Only one agent at a time can take control of the emulator. 2. The worktree creation, all git operations and PR information is deterministic and handled by the harness taking into consideration how Android projects are built. 3. Open the worktree in Android Studio. 4. Open the emulator from the TUI.

Caveats: For now it only works for Claude Code.

title.value: Show HN: An open-source harness for Android devs in the terminal

story_text.value:
Hey HN, we’re Nel and Kosi.

We noticed personal agents like Instinct, Muse were terrible at buying stuff. Most of the time the checkout would fail.

So we built reliable automations for agents to checkout at 9 leading grocery merchants.

We grapple with anti bot, logins, OTP codes, and changing checkout structures.

Loved revisiting this stuff given our backgrounds sneaker-botting and building computer use models. Honestly full circle haha.

It currently works on these sites with ~70% checkout success rate:

- Walmart - Albertsons - Ocado - Wegmans - FreshDirect - Best Buy - Instacart

Our goal is to hill climb to 90%+ across each.

Test keys are free and run the real flow without placing an order.

New accounts get 10 free completed orders.

https://docs.getagentmall.com/quickstart

story_text.value:
I like listening to rain and I like maps, so I built a physics-based simulator of how rain sounds on different surfaces and linked it up to a live weather map.

You can pick any place on the map and play what the rain there would sound like right now, driven by live weather data. It grew into a whole soundscape: thunder, wind, seasonally appropriate birds, insects, frogs, the sea, vehicles and other urban sounds. The sound is binaural, so with headphones it has some spatial depth.

Only the birds are recordings (from xeno-canto, with attribution). Every other environmental sound is synthesized in your browser by a C++ engine compiled WebAssembly.

There's also a live radio that tunes to real local stations near wherever you are on the map. It gets mixed with the environmental sounds and you can adjust it to sound like it's coming from far away. Nearby storms can add crackle to the radio signal.

The radar map comes from my own tile server. It uses raw public radar data where available and falls back to satellite otherwise.

I'd love to hear feedback!

title.value: Show HN: It's Raining Somewhere – hear live simulated weather anywhere on Earth

story_text.value:
Hi HN! I'm Matthew, a software engineer tired of paid budgeting apps doing fuzzy averages and making me categorize every card swipe.

Example: which category is Rent on the 1st? Which category is my $114 "Valuemart" purchase last week? It doesn't matter IMO. What matters is that Rent repeats every 1st, I have $218 left for spending until Friday, and I can contribute $500 to my Roth IRA next paycheck and have $2,000 left in that account.

Bills just cost what they cost, and I need to see exactly when they will come out and how much money that leaves me on that day.

For spending, I just move a hunk of cash to a separate "safe to spend" account every Friday and try not to blow through it. This means I can see exactly when spending money will come out too, and how much money that leaves me. I might spend more on gas this week and more for the party next week; there's no 'normal' week. It sounds simple, but it took me years of trial and error to find this system that consistently works for me and make a halfway-decent app to track it.

Cashcraft is free, and doesn't require an account to start locally. If you do sign up, your data is end-to-end encrypted. Bank sync is built but not public yet, because it costs money via Plaid, but you can import transactions from your bank. I might add it as a paid feature later. I wish bank sync could be free, but integrating with 100s of legacy bank systems necessarily costs Plaid money, which makes them charge implementers money.

If you're interested, give it a try and let me know what you like or don't about it. I'd like to improve it. Thank you!

title.value: Show HN: Cashcraft – free precise budgeting without categories
